She was diagnosed with contact dermatitis at a walk-in clinic. Over days 4–9, she developed a right earache and headache and the rash spread to her upper right chest-wall.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 54-year-old female developed right-sided neck pain on day 1, followed by an erythematous vesicular rash on the right anterior chest, neck, and shoulder in the C2-C4 dermatomes by day 4, initially misdiagnosed as contact dermatitis. Between days 4 and 9, she developed right earache and headache, and the rash spread. At the ER, on day 9, RHS was clinically diagnosed based on the evolving symptoms and characteristic rash, and treatment with valacyclovir extended to 10 days plus prednisone was initiated. By day 14, she developed partial right-sided facial paralysis consistent with cranial nerve VII involvement of RHS. Follow-up by day 46 showed significant clinical improvement with symmetric facial movements and eye closure. No laboratory confirmation of VZV or detailed audiovestibular testing results were documented in the source reports.
